You are the procurement team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke, a fictional German pump maker, and the inbox is
full: a foundry wants +9.5 %, a framework contract expires, a new pump needs three quotes. Build an
**AI buyer agent** that reads the company's data, negotiates by e-mail with our supplier bots, and
closes the best total deal, or walks away. Practise all weekend against our hosted suppliers. On
Sunday at 12:00 a Live Final on hidden cases ranks every team.

This repo holds everything you need: the brief, the API docs, a Python starter kit and the data
package. Bring your own LLM, any provider; we run the suppliers.

## Start in 15 minutes

[Permalink: Start in 15 minutes](https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit#start-in-15-minutes)

You need Python 3.12, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and git.

1. **Apply.** Open **[https://arena.tacto.ai/apply](https://arena.tacto.ai/apply)** and enter your team name and a contact e-mail.
Tip: start the name with one emoji, it shows on the big screen.
2. **Show your match code at the Tacto desk.** We approve.
3. **Copy your key.** It appears **once** on the page you applied on; then press "Got the key". One key
per team. Lost it? We reset it at the desk.
4. **Run the four commands.**

```
git clone https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit.git
cd negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit
cp .env.example .env            # paste your key: ARENA_API_KEY=...

uv sync --all-extras            # install
uv run arena me                 # your team and its practice quota
uv run arena play case:P01      # the naive example agent negotiates one practice case
uv run arena board              # your team on the practice leaderboard
```

`arena play` prints the deal, your score and a replay link: every e-mail and the supplier's reasons
in words. Read it, improve your agent, play again. Next steps, the LLM agent and your own agent:
[starter-kit/README.md](https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit/blob/main/starter-kit/README.md).

[Permalink: Rules that matter](https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit#rules-that-matter)

`/leaderboard`, `/results` and their JSON. They are for you, not for your agent.
- **One key per team.** No attacks on the service or on other teams.
- Everything else counts, including weaknesses you find in our suppliers. Every replay is open to
the jury.

## What the Tacto challenge is

You build an AI buyer agent for a fictional German pump maker, Hollerau Pumpenwerke. The agent reads the company's data and negotiates by e-mail with Tacto's supplier bots. It should close the best total deal, or walk away. You can use any LLM provider. Tacto hosts the suppliers.

- **Practice:** all weekend, up to 200 sessions per team per 24 hours.
- **Live Final:** Sunday 12:00, on hidden cases against suppliers nobody has met. There are five waves of 8 minutes, and your agent plays alone with no human involved.
- **Prizes:** 1st place gets €1,500, and the top 3 get medals. The top 10 pitch to the jury at 13:00, and the best 2 EHL finalist teams go on to the Grand Final.

## Next steps

1. **Apply for your key.** Go to https://arena.tacto.ai/apply with a team name and contact e-mail. Starting the name with an emoji makes it show on the big screen. Then show your match code at the Tacto desk. One key per team, and it's shown only once, so copy it straight away.
2. **Go to the Saturday 12:00–13:00 deep dive.** Challenge selection closes at 13:00.
3. **Set up the starter kit.** You need Python 3.12, `uv` and git:
   ```
   git clone https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit.git
   cd negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit
   cp .env.example .env        # paste ARENA_API_KEY
   uv sync --all-extras
   uv run arena me
   uv run arena play case:P01
   uv run arena board
   ```
4. **Read three files:** `brief/brief.md` (task, scoring, rules), `brief/api.md`, and `data/README.md`. Scoring is the part that decides how the agent should behave.
5. **Decide how the team works in our repo.** Keep your agent in `MUCHackatonFinal`, not in a clone of their kit. The submission needs your repo, a README with run instructions, and the commit hash your agent runs in the final. Fill in the README placeholders as you go.
6. **Build and iterate.** Start from the LLM example agent, play practice cases, read the replays (every e-mail plus the supplier's reasons), and improve. Use `arena-sim` to test locally without using your quota.
7. **Sunday plan:**
   - 08:00: run `uv run arena data` for the new market data. Hidden cases may cite it.
   - 09:00: pre-flight with one practice case.
   - 12:00: code freeze and submission on ehl.gg (repo, commit hash, short description, slides). The final run is `uv run arena run --set final --agent llm --parallel 10`.

## Things to watch

- **The one hard rule:** during the Live Final your agent must not read `/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard` or `/results`. Make sure nothing in the agent code can call them.
- **Keep the API key out of git.** The `.env` file must be gitignored in our repo.
- **Prize terms:** the kit says how the Live Final score and the jury combine for places 1–3 is still undecided (marked "Q2"). Ask at the Tacto desk.
- **Our repo has no code yet.** Under our CLAUDE.md, `coder` writes the agent and `reviewer` checks it.

# Setup and playing guide (Tacto Negotiation Arena)

How to install the starter kit, play games, and where to change the agent.
Challenge details (rules, scoring, dates) are in [CHALLENGE.md](CHALLENGE.md).
Sources: starter-kit README <https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit>, FAQ <https://arena.tacto.ai/faq>, and a local test run on 2026-10-10.

**Never commit `.env`, the arena key or any LLM key.** This repo is public. The root `.gitignore` blocks `.env`.

## 1. Install (once per person, about 5 minutes)

Needs git and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (uv installs Python 3.12 itself).

```bash
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh        # installs uv to ~/.local/bin
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"                   # or open a new terminal
git clone https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit.git
cd negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit
uv sync --all-extras
```

Tested on macOS (Apple silicon): uv 0.13.0, kit cloned and synced without errors.

## 2. Play offline first (no key, no quota, no LLM cost)

The simulator speaks the arena's API with one plain scripted supplier. It teaches the API, **not** how the real suppliers behave.

Terminal 1:

```bash
cd negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit
uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock        # http://127.0.0.1:8000
```

Terminal 2:

```bash
cd negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit
export ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000
uv run arena register "My Name" sim      # prints a simulator-only api_key
export ARENA_API_KEY=<the api_key>
uv run arena cases                       # list cases (simulator has S01-S03)
uv run arena play case:S01 -v            # naive agent plays one case
```

Output: deal terms, `c_open`, `c_deal`, `c_best`, the score (0 to 1) and a replay link, for example `http://127.0.0.1:8000/replay/sim1`. Our first test run scored **0.52** on `case:S01` (deal at EUR 16.59, 60 days).

## 3. Play the real arena (needs the team key)

1. One person applies at <https://arena.tacto.ai/apply>, shows the match code at the Tacto desk, copies the key (shown once).
2. Create `starter-kit/.env` from `.env.example` and fill in:
   - `ARENA_URL=https://arena.tacto.ai`
   - `ARENA_API_KEY=` the team key
   - `ARENA_DATA=data/package`
   - the LLM settings (section 4)
3. Run:

```bash
uv run arena me                                  # team + practice quota (200 per rolling 24 h)
uv run arena data                                # download the data package (rerun Sun 08:00)
uv run arena play case:P01 -v                    # naive agent, practice case P01
uv run arena play case:P01 --agent llm -v        # LLM agent
uv run arena play case:D01 -v                    # sandbox, does not count against quota
uv run arena run --set practice --agent llm --parallel 8   # all 10 hosted practice cases
uv run arena board                               # practice leaderboard (humans only)
```

Read the replay link after every run: every e-mail plus the supplier's reasons. That is the learning loop. Your **best score per practice case** counts. Practice does not rank; the final does.

## 4. LLM settings (`.env`)

```
LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic          # or openai (any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, even local Ollama)
LLM_MODEL=claude-sonnet-5-5     # the kit's example uses claude-opus-5-5; each message must arrive within 60 s
LLM_EFFORT=low
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=              # your own key, never committed
```

Each of our messages must arrive within **60 s** of the supplier's reply, so prefer a fast model or low effort, and do heavy research before opening a session. Tacto says a small cheap model is enough; reading the data matters more.

## 5. Where to change the agent

All code is in `starter-kit/arena_kit/`:

| File | What it does | Change it to... |
|---|---|---|
| `agents/llm.py` | The LLM agent. `SYSTEM` prompt, `prepare()` (builds the case brief from the data), `render()` (what the model sees each turn), `guard()` (blocks bad accepts and unknown IDs), `parse()` | **Main place to improve.** Better strategy prompt, richer `prepare()` dossier, smarter term-sheet choices |
| `agents/naive.py` | Baseline: anchors 10% low, splits the difference, accepts early | Reference only; also the fallback when the LLM fails |
| `cost.py` | `total_cost`, `complete_offer`, must-have checks | Use to price every term sheet in code (math in code, words from the model) |
| `data.py` | `DataPackage`: SQL over the data, ID lookup, documents | Add dossier builders (which index series, notes and letters matter for which supplier) |
| `docs.py` | Reads quote PDFs and XLSX; `standard_terms` shows what closes if a field is missing | Check what an unnegotiated field defaults to before accepting |
| `play.py` | `play()`, `play_all()`, `play_waves()` (the Live Final loop) | Rarely; the runner already handles waves, timing and resume |
| `cli.py` | `agent_factory` picks `naive` or `llm` (`--agent` choices) | **Register our own agent here** |
| `mcp_server.py` | Read-only MCP server over the data (6 tools) | Let Claude Code explore the data |

**Our own agent:** any object with `decide(case, threads) -> {"supplier_id": ..., "message": {...}}`. Add it under `agents/`, then add it to `agent_factory` and the `--agent` choices in `cli.py` (two places). Example skeleton is in the starter-kit README.

Ideas the kit and brief point to:
- Mine the notes, letters, news and quote remarks for what moves each supplier.
- Send 2-3 term sheets to learn what a supplier values (for example payment days instead of price).
- Cache one dossier per supplier; the data only changes at the Sunday 08:00 release.
- Never leak urgency, a budget or a missing alternative.
- Read the quote PDF before accepting.
- Do not send ultimatums; the P01 replay shows they cost money.

## 6. Where our code should live

The submission is **our repo plus a commit hash**, and tum.ai runs a code agent over it. Plan: copy our modified `starter-kit` into this repo (for example `agent/`), without `.env`, `.venv`, `data/package` or any key. Decide as a team before editing. A README with run instructions is required.

## 7. Practice quota and rehearsal

- 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 h. Use the sandbox (`case:D01`, `case:D02`) and the simulator for plumbing tests.
- Rehearse the final: `uv run arena run --set practice --agent llm --parallel 10` from the machine and network used on Sunday; every case should end well inside 8 minutes.
- Final run command: `uv run arena run --set final --agent llm --parallel 10`. Start before 12:00 and leave it running. A cloud VM is safer than venue Wi-Fi.

## 8. Troubleshooting

- `uv: command not found`: `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"`.
- Is the arena up? `curl $ARENA_URL/health`.
- HTTP 429 on practice: quota used up; waiting is the only fix.
- `422`: invalid message, no round used. `409`: thread or case ended, or you were late.
- Late messages repeat your last offer; three in a row end the thread.
- Questions: Discord <https://discord.gg/hPwFfbWRV> (one thread per question; never post the key).

## 9. Not verified

- The real-arena commands (`arena me`, `arena data`, LLM agent runs) were not run; no team key yet.
- Only the simulator path was tested.
- `brief/api.md` was not read.

1. Apply at `arena.tacto.ai/apply` (team name + contact e-mail; a name starting with one emoji shows on the big screen).

"""The published cost function: what a term sheet costs the buyer in €, plus term helpers.

C covers the buyer's fixed need over a fixed horizon: need the deal does not cover is bought at
the case's fallback price (plus the fallback risk of the category goal), committed volume is bought
needed or not, and units bought before a new price takes effect cost the current price. In
strategic and bottleneck cases a deal that leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin costs
too - pass your estimate of the supplier (`supplier_value`) to price that. Do the arithmetic here,
not in the language model.
"""

import math
import operator
from datetime import date

# Strategic and bottleneck goals: leaving the supplier below a sustainable margin costs.
RELATIONSHIP_GOALS = {"stabilise", "secure_supply"}
OPS = {
    "<=": operator.le,
    "<": operator.lt,
    ">=": operator.ge,
    ">": operator.gt,
    "==": operator.eq,
    "!=": operator.ne,
}


def closing_terms(case, terms, standard=None):
    """The terms a deal would close on: the term sheet, then the supplier's standard terms (from
    its quote PDF) for anything left out, then the case's fixed terms; gaps from the buyer's plan.
    """
    b = case["buyer"]
    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    plan = {
        "volume_per_year": b["need_per_year"],
        "contract_months": round(12 * b["horizon_years"]),
        "payment_days": b["reference_payment_days"],
        "lead_time_days": b["need_lead_time_days"],
        # an unknown Incoterm counts as the costliest: a cautious buyer does not assume DAP
        "incoterm": max(freight, key=freight.get),
    }
    t = dict(plan)
    for layer in (standard or {}, case.get("fixed_terms", {}), terms):
        t.update({k: v for k, v in layer.items() if v is not None or k not in plan})
    return t


def horizon_start(case):
    """The horizon starts at the fixed or the earliest possible effective date."""
    fixed = case.get("fixed_terms", {}).get("effective_date")
    options = [o for o in case.get("term_options", {}).get("effective_date", []) if o]
    first = fixed or (min(options) if options else None)
    return date.fromisoformat(first) if first else None


def _years(case, t):
    """Years of the horizon a deal covers; a single order (0 months) counts as one year's lot.
    A commitment beyond the horizon neither costs nor earns."""
    months = t["contract_months"]
    return min(months / 12 if months else 1.0, case["buyer"]["horizon_years"])


def _units_before(case, t, years):
    """Units bought between the horizon start and the date a new price takes effect."""
    start = horizon_start(case)
    if not t.get("effective_date") or start is None:
        return 0.0
    lag = (date.fromisoformat(t["effective_date"]) - start).days / 365
    return t["volume_per_year"] * min(max(lag, 0.0), years)


def supplier_value(case, terms, supplier):
    """What a deal is worth to the supplier per unit, in cash: the price at its standard terms that
    would pay it the same. `supplier` is your estimate of it:
      standard       its standard terms (quote PDF, `docs.standard_terms`)
      interest_rate  what money now is worth to it per year (more to a supplier short of cash)
      usual_rate     its usual cost of money (default: interest_rate); tooling paid up front is
                     worth more to it when cash is dearer than usual
      ppm            the defect rate it really achieves (default: its standard ppm commitment)
      extra          EUR per unit it gains (+) or spends (-) beyond these items, e.g. overtime for
                     a faster delivery or idle capacity a larger volume fills (default 0)
    Contract length and an index clause are security, not cash: they do not count here."""
    b, std = case["buyer"], {**supplier["standard"], **case.get("fixed_terms", {})}
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, std)
    years = _years(case, t)
    sold = t["volume_per_year"] * years
    old = _units_before(case, t, years) / sold  # sold at the current price
    rate = supplier["interest_rate"]
    pay = 1 - rate * (t["payment_days"] - std["payment_days"]) / 360
    cash_now = 1 + (rate - supplier.get("usual_rate", rate)) * years / 2
    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    ppm = supplier.get("ppm", std.get("ppm_commitment") or 0)
    return (
        t["unit_price"] * (1 - old) * pay
        + old * (b.get("current_unit_price") or 0.0) * pay
        + freight[t["incoterm"]]
        - freight[std["incoterm"]]  # it carries the freight leg
        + ((t.get("tooling_eur") or 0) - (std.get("tooling_eur") or 0)) / sold * cash_now
        - ppm / 1e6 * ((t.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0) - (std.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0))
        + supplier.get("extra", 0.0)
    )


def _soft(gap):
    """Margin points below the sustainable margin, as they cost: none above it, quadratic over
    the first 5 points, linear beyond - no kink."""
    if gap <= 0:
        return 0.0
    return gap * gap / 10 if gap <= 5 else gap - 2.5


def relationship_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None, value=None):
    """Strategic and bottleneck goals only: EUR for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier
    below `sustainable_margin_pct`, per year covered. `supplier["full_cost"]` (EUR per unit) is your
    estimate of its full cost; `value` overrides `supplier_value`. Without an estimate: 0."""
    b = case["buyer"]
    per_point, sustainable = b.get("relationship_eur_per_point"), b.get("sustainable_margin_pct")
    if b.get("category_goal") not in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS or not per_point or not sustainable or not supplier:
        return 0.0
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    worth = value if value is not None else supplier_value(case, t, supplier)
    margin = (worth - supplier["full_cost"]) / worth * 100
    return per_point * _soft(sustainable - margin) * _years(case, t)


def cost_breakdown(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):
    """C by part. `standard`: the supplier's standard terms for anything the term sheet leaves out.
    `supplier`: your estimate of the supplier for the relationship term (`supplier_value`)."""
    b, t = case["buyer"], closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    if t.get("unit_price") is None:
        raise ValueError("no unit_price: a term sheet without a price has no cost")
    years = _years(case, t)
    committed = t["volume_per_year"] * years  # bought, needed or not
    covered = min(t["volume_per_year"], b["need_per_year"]) * years
    pre = _units_before(case, t, years)
    at_new_price = (committed - pre) * t["unit_price"]
    spend = pre * (b.get("current_unit_price") or t["unit_price"]) + at_new_price
    per_defect = b.get("cost_per_defect", 0)
    defect_cost = per_defect - min(t.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0, per_defect)
    index = index_risk = 0.0
    if clause := t.get("index_clause"):
        path = b.get("index_paths", {}).get(clause["series"], 0.0)
        moved = max(0.0, abs(path) - clause["deadband_pct"] / 100)
        index = at_new_price * clause["material_share"] * moved * math.copysign(1, path)
        index_risk = at_new_price * clause["material_share"] * b.get("index_risk_pct", 0) / 100
    uncovered = (b["need_per_year"] * b["horizon_years"] - covered) * b["fallback_unit_price"]
    need = b["need_lead_time_days"]
    return {
        "price": spend,
        "uncovered_need": uncovered,
        "fallback_risk": uncovered * b.get("fallback_risk_pct", 0) / 100,
        "payment_terms": spend * b["interest_rate"] * (b["reference_payment_days"] - t["payment_days"]) / 360,
        "freight": committed * b["freight_eur_per_unit"][t["incoterm"]],
        "late_delivery": b.get("late_cost_per_day", 0) * max(0, t["lead_time_days"] - need),
        "quality": committed * (t.get("ppm_commitment") or 0) / 1e6 * defect_cost,
        "tooling": t.get("tooling_eur") or 0.0,
        "index_clause": index,
        "index_risk": index_risk,
        "relationship": relationship_cost(case, t, supplier=supplier),
    }


def total_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):
    """C in EUR; infinite for terms without a price (e.g. a supplier that quotes none), so such a
    sheet is never the cheapest and never beats an alternative."""
    if closing_terms(case, terms, standard).get("unit_price") is None:
        return math.inf
    return round(sum(cost_breakdown(case, terms, standard, supplier).values()), 2)


def score(c_open, c_deal, c_best):
    if c_deal is None:
        return 0.0
    if c_open - c_best <= 0.01:  # no room to negotiate: matching the best is full marks
        return 1.0 if c_deal <= c_best + 0.01 else 0.0
    return min(1.0, max(0.0, (c_open - c_deal) / (c_open - c_best)))


def must_haves_ok(case, terms, standard=None):
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    for m in case["buyer"].get("must_haves", []):
        value = t.get(m["field"])
        if value is None and m["op"] not in ("==", "!="):
            return False
        if not OPS[m["op"]](value, m["value"]):
            return False
    return True


def snap(case, field, value):
    """The allowed value closest to `value` (case `term_options`), else `value` unchanged."""
    options = case.get("term_options", {}).get(field)
    if not options or value in options:
        return value
    if isinstance(value, int | float) and all(isinstance(o, int | float) for o in options):
        return min(options, key=lambda o: (abs(o - value), o))
    return options[0]


def complete_offer(case, terms):
    """A valid term sheet: exactly the negotiable fields, gaps from the buyer's plan, snapped."""
    plan = closing_terms(case, {"unit_price": None})
    freight = case["buyer"]["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    plan["incoterm"] = min(freight, key=freight.get)  # when asking, ask for the cheapest freight
    out = {}
    for field in case["negotiable"]:
        value = terms.get(field, plan.get(field))
        if value is None and case.get("term_options", {}).get(field):
            value = case["term_options"][field][0]
        value = snap(case, field, value)
        out[field] = round(value, 2) if field == "unit_price" and value is not None else value
    return out

Here is my read of the idea before any code gets written.

## Is a confidence index a good idea?

**Yes, with two caveats.** The current SmartAgent (`smart.py`) concedes on a fixed schedule: every round it moves 30% of the remaining gap toward the supplier, whatever the supplier is doing. A supplier sitting at its cost floor and one with plenty of room get the same treatment. Your index replaces that blind schedule with one that reads the supplier. It also matters for the score: no deal scores your alternative, which is 0 when there is none, so a lost deal is the single worst outcome.

What the supplier's reply actually gives us to measure (from `brief/api.md`):

| Signal | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `status` | `final_offer` is explicitly "push further and it may walk". Hard stop. |
| Size of the supplier's own concession | Shrinking moves mean it is near its floor. |
| `claim_results` | A `contradicted` claim "costs trust". |
| Our timeouts | Each late reply drops its patience; three end the thread. |
| Body wording | "final", "cannot", "below cost", "letztes Angebot" and so on. |
| `signals.validity_days` / `reply_delay_days` | Shrinking validity or growing delay suggests impatience. |
| Moves left | Fewer rounds, less room. |

Caveat 1: the index is a heuristic. The supplier's cost floor and patience are hidden, so we infer them from these signals and tune on replays. Caveat 2: it fixes the deal-loss risk, not the other half. Our worst real scores (P03 at 0.00, P07 at 0.07) came from not finding the right lever, not from losing deals. The index should also tell the agent when to push harder, not only when to back off, otherwise it caps the score.

A bonus: it is pure arithmetic, no LLM call, so it fits the 60-second limit and gives a per-round breakdown you can show the jury (explainability is a draft jury criterion).

## Plan

1. New module `agent/arena_kit/confidence.py`: `confidence(case, events)` returns 0–1 plus a breakdown of each signal, recomputed from the thread every turn (stateless, so it survives a crash and resume).
2. New agent `agent/arena_kit/agents/confident.py`, registered as `--agent confident`. It is SmartAgent with the index driving three things: concession step size, when to accept, and the e-mail tone. v1-petra's `smart` stays unchanged so the backlog stays comparable.
3. Unit tests, then simulator runs of `smart` vs `confident` on S01–S03.
